### Analysis of CyCIF tonsil dataset for "Are low-variance Principal Components of single-cell omics data biologically meaningful, or just noise?"
### Data source. 
#https://elifesciences.org/articles/31657#content

### Runs main analysis: PCA on 30 channels; spatial correlation by neighbour rank within and between sections (1000 nearest neighbours); exponential fits; predicted noise fraction per PC from repeat-stained markers
### Inputs: TONSILA_aligned_corrected.csv TONSILB_reordered_corrected.csv
### Outputs: Panels for figure 1. 

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

### libraries 

```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library(cowplot)
library(ggplot2)
```

### functions 
```{r}

### Find NN, return NN index and distances 
find_neighbours_with_dist <- function(datA_centroids, query_coords, k, drop_self = TRUE) {
  extra <- if (drop_self) 1L else 0L  
  ### If drop_self is TRUE, find one extra neighbour, because the cell itself is returned first
  knn <- RANN::nn2(data = as.matrix(datA_centroids),
                   query = as.matrix(query_coords), k = k + extra)
  if (drop_self) {  ### Drop the first NN if drop self is true. so that within section queries do not count a cell as its own NN.
    list(idx  = knn$nn.idx[, -1, drop = FALSE],
         dist = knn$nn.dists[, -1, drop = FALSE])
    ### If doing between sections do not drop one 
  } else {
    list(idx  = knn$nn.idx,
         dist = knn$nn.dists)
  }
}

### PC-level spatial correlation at each neighbour rank 
pc_correlation <- function(x_scores, y_scores_full, neighbour_pairs) {
  ### Get number of PC and number of NN
  num_pcs <- ncol(x_scores); k <- ncol(neighbour_pairs)
  cor_matrix <- matrix(NA, num_pcs, k,
    dimnames = list(colnames(x_scores), paste0("Neighbor", 1:k)))
  for (p in 1:num_pcs) {
    x <- x_scores[, p]
    for (c in 1:k) {
      ### Correlation, across cells, between each cell's PC score and the score of its neighbour at this rank.
      y <- y_scores_full[neighbour_pairs[, c], p]
      cor_matrix[p, c] <- cor(x, y, use = "complete.obs")
    }
  }
  cor_matrix
}


### Returns the decay-curve plot for one PC (within and between sections), with its legend; x is the mean distance at each neighbour rank
make_pc_plot <- function(pc) {

  ### Observed correlation at each neighbour rank, for the three pairings
  decay_df_pc <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(pair = "A → A", dist = mean_d_AA, cor = as.numeric(cAA[pc, ])),
    data.frame(pair = "A → B", dist = mean_d_AB, cor = as.numeric(cAB[pc, ])),
    data.frame(pair = "B → B", dist = mean_d_BB, cor = as.numeric(cBB[pc, ]))
  )

  ### Fitted exponential curve for each pairing
  ft_pc  <- fit_table[fit_table$PC == pc, ]
  fit_df <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ft_pc)), function(i) {
    row <- ft_pc[i, ]
    if (is.na(row$A) || is.na(row$lambda)) return(NULL)
    pair_label <- gsub("->", "→", row$pair)
    d_range <- decay_df_pc$dist[decay_df_pc$pair == pair_label]
    d_seq   <- seq(min(d_range), max(d_range), length.out = 200)
    data.frame(pair = pair_label, dist = d_seq,
               cor = row$A * exp(-d_seq / row$lambda))
  }))

  ggplot(decay_df_pc, aes(x = dist, y = cor, colour = pair)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.2, alpha = 0.7, stroke = 0.8) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_lims, xlim = x_lims) +
    geom_line(data = fit_df, aes(x = dist, y = cor, group = pair),
              inherit.aes = FALSE,
              colour = "red", linetype = 6, linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("A → A" = "grey40", "B → B" = "#E07B54", "A → B" = "#3D7EA6")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
    labs(x = "Distance (μm)", y = "Correlation") +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray90", linetype = "solid", linewidth = 0.12),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80", linetype = "solid", linewidth = 0.23)
    )
}


### Fit an exponential decay curve to a correlation decay curve  
### Fit C(d) = A * exp(-d / L), where A is the correlation amplitude and L is the length scale.
fit_exponential_decay <- function(dist, corr) {
  df_fit <- data.frame(d = dist, corr = as.numeric(corr)) %>%
    filter(is.finite(corr), is.finite(d))
  if (nrow(df_fit) < 10) return(c(A=NA, lambda=NA, A_se=NA, lambda_se=NA))
  #### Starting value for L: the distance at which the correlation is closest to 1/e of its maximum, with a minimum of 5 µm
  corr_thresh <- max(df_fit$corr) / exp(1)
  L_start <- df_fit$d[which.min(abs(df_fit$corr - corr_thresh))]
  L_start <- max(L_start, 5)
  
  fit <- tryCatch(
    nls(corr ~ A * exp(-d / L), data = df_fit,
        ### Initialize A as the maximum observed correlation.  
        start = list(A = max(df_fit$corr), L = L_start),
        lower = c(A = -1, L = min(df_fit$d)),
        upper = c(A = 1, L = max(df_fit$d)),
        algorithm = "port"),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  
  ### fallback if first attempt fails
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      nls(corr ~ A * exp(-d / L), data = df_fit,
          start = list(A = 0.01, L = 100),
          lower = c(A = -1, L = min(df_fit$d)),
          upper = c(A = 1, L = max(df_fit$d)),
          algorithm = "port"),
      error = function(e) NULL)
  }
  ### return outputs
  if (is.null(fit)) return(c(A=NA, lambda=NA, A_se=NA, lambda_se=NA))
  sm <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  c(A = sm["A","Estimate"], lambda = sm["L","Estimate"],
    A_se = sm["A","Std. Error"], lambda_se = sm["L","Std. Error"])
}

### Helper function to feed all the PC into the fitting function 
fit_all_pcs <- function(cor_mat, mean_d, pair_name) {

  out <- lapply(rownames(cor_mat), function(pc) {

    params <- fit_exponential_decay(mean_d, cor_mat[pc, ])

    data.frame(
      PC       = pc,
      pair     = pair_name,
      A        = params["A"],
      lambda   = params["lambda"],
      A_se     = params["A_se"],
      lambda_se = params["lambda_se"],
      row.names = NULL
    )
  })

  do.call(rbind, out)
}

```

### 1. Load flat-field corrected, affine aligned and reordered data from scripts 01-03  
```{r}
#### load flat-field  corrected, affine aligned and reordered data  
A_reg_trimmed<- read.csv("Data/TONSILA_aligned_corrected.csv")



tonsilB_trimmed <- read.csv("Data/TONSILB_reordered_corrected.csv")

### The 48 marker channels (columns 17 to 64)
marker_cols <- names(A_reg_trimmed)[17:64]

```


```{r}
### Pull out flat-field corrected markers and rename 


A_bf_markers <-  A_reg_trimmed[, grep("_bf", colnames(A_reg_trimmed), value = TRUE)]



B_bf_markers <- tonsilB_trimmed[, grep("_bf", colnames(tonsilB_trimmed), value = TRUE)]


### Remove the _bf suffix so column names match the channel names 
colnames(A_bf_markers) <- sub("_bf", "", colnames(A_bf_markers))
colnames(B_bf_markers) <- sub("_bf", "", colnames(B_bf_markers))


```


### 2. Filter data and run PCA 
```{r}
###  Exclude auto-fluorescence channels, repeated reference stains, and channels that failed QC
###### Channels dropped for quality reasons (staining artefacts, poor signal quality, or late-cycle tissue loss
drop_sus <- c("Cy3_15", "Cy5_5", "Cy3_4", "FITC_5", "Cy3_9", "Cy5_15")
#### repeat measurements of PCNA, Vimentin, and Tubulin
drop_ref <- c("FITC_7", "Cy3_7", "Cy5_7", "FITC_12", "Cy3_12", "Cy5_12",
              "FITC_16", "Cy3_16", "Cy5_16")
### auto-fluorescence
drop_af <- c("FITC_1", "Cy3_1", "Cy5_1")
drop_all <- c(drop_sus, drop_ref, drop_af)
keep_30 <- setdiff(marker_cols, drop_all)


### Keep the 30 retained channels
A_markers_for_pc <- A_bf_markers[, keep_30]
B_markers_for_pc <- B_bf_markers[, keep_30]

### Center but do not scale the markers 
A_centered <- scale(A_markers_for_pc, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
B_centered <- scale(B_markers_for_pc, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

###  PCA on the centered Tonsil A data, without scaling
pca <- prcomp(A_centered, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)

### PCA scores for Tonsil A
sA <- pca$x


### PCA is fit on Tonsil A, and Tonsil B is projected using the Tonsil A loading
sB <- B_centered %*% pca$rotation
colnames(sA) <- paste0("PC", 1:ncol(sA))
colnames(sB) <- paste0("PC", 1:ncol(sB))


### Variance explained by each pc
var_explained = pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)
```

### 3. Calculate within- and between-section spatial correlation 
```{r}
### Spatial correlations (within and between sections) 

### Number of nearest neighbours
k_max <- 1000
### Create matrix of single cell coordinates  
coords_A_raw <- as.matrix(A_reg_trimmed[, c("Xt", "Yt")])
coords_A_aff <- as.matrix(A_reg_trimmed[, c("Xt_aff", "Yt_aff")])
coords_B_raw <- as.matrix(tonsilB_trimmed[, c("Xt", "Yt")])

### Find the NN for within sections and between sections  using affine aligned coordinates for A -> B 
nb_AA <- find_neighbours_with_dist(coords_A_raw, coords_A_raw,
                                   k_max, drop_self = TRUE)

nb_AB <- find_neighbours_with_dist(coords_B_raw, coords_A_aff,
                                   k_max, drop_self = FALSE)

nb_BB <- find_neighbours_with_dist(coords_B_raw, coords_B_raw,
                                   k_max, drop_self = TRUE)
 

### Mean distance at each neighbour rank (the x axis of the decay curves)
mean_d_AA <- colMeans(nb_AA$dist)
mean_d_AB <- colMeans(nb_AB$dist)
mean_d_BB <- colMeans(nb_BB$dist)


### For each PC, calculate the Pearson correlation between cell scores and neighbour scores at each neighbour rank.
cAA <- pc_correlation(sA, sA, nb_AA$idx)
cAB <- pc_correlation(sA, sB, nb_AB$idx)
cBB <- pc_correlation(sB, sB, nb_BB$idx)
```




### 4. Fit exponential decay curves to each pc for between and within sections
```{r}
### fits using C(d) = A·exp(−d/L), with bounds of A between −1 and 1, and L between the smallest and largest distance.
fit_table <- rbind(
  fit_all_pcs(cAA, mean_d_AA, "A -> A"),
  fit_all_pcs(cAB, mean_d_AB, "A -> B"),
  fit_all_pcs(cBB, mean_d_BB, "B -> B"))


### add PC number for plotting 
fit_table$pc_num <- as.numeric(gsub("PC", "", fit_table$PC))

```

### 8. Noise estimation and make figure 1A (Estimated noise fraction of each PC)

```{r}
### Loss for estimating r_1…r_4, where r_i is the correlation of repeat i with the true signal. The model correlation matrix has off-diagonal elements r_i·r_j; loss = log det Σ + tr(SΣ⁻¹), with S the observed correlation matrix. r = tanh(z) keeps each r between −1 and 1.
### Each repeat is the true signal plus independent noise, so the correlation between repeats i and j is r_i × r_j.
loss_function_z4 <- function(z, S) {
  r <- tanh(z)
  Sigma <- matrix(c(
    1,         r[1]*r[2], r[1]*r[3], r[1]*r[4],
    r[1]*r[2], 1,         r[2]*r[3], r[2]*r[4],
    r[1]*r[3], r[2]*r[3], 1,         r[3]*r[4],
    r[1]*r[4], r[2]*r[4], r[3]*r[4], 1
  ), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)

  inv_Sigma <- solve(Sigma)
  logdet    <- determinant(Sigma, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus
  tr_term   <- sum(S * inv_Sigma)
  loss      <- as.numeric(logdet + tr_term)
  return(loss)
}
### PCNA, Vimentin, and Tubulin were each measured four times in both sections.

pcna_A_cov <- cov(as.matrix(A_bf_markers[, paste0("FITC_", c(3, 7, 12, 16))]))
vim_A_cov  <- cov(as.matrix(A_bf_markers[, paste0("Cy3_",  c(3, 7, 12, 16))]))
tub_A_cov  <- cov(as.matrix(A_bf_markers[, paste0("Cy5_",  c(3, 7, 12, 16))]))

pcna_B_cov <- cov(as.matrix(B_bf_markers[, paste0("FITC_", c(3, 7, 12, 16))]))
vim_B_cov  <- cov(as.matrix(B_bf_markers[, paste0("Cy3_",  c(3, 7, 12, 16))]))
tub_B_cov  <- cov(as.matrix(B_bf_markers[, paste0("Cy5_",  c(3, 7, 12, 16))]))

### Pairwise repeat correlations are used to estimate technical-noise variance
pcna_A_cor <- cov2cor(pcna_A_cov)
vim_A_cor  <- cov2cor(vim_A_cov)
tub_A_cor  <- cov2cor(tub_A_cov)

pcna_B_cor <- cov2cor(pcna_B_cov)
vim_B_cor  <- cov2cor(vim_B_cov)
tub_B_cor  <- cov2cor(tub_B_cov)
### For each marker and section, fit the four r values to the six pairwise correlations. 
### Noise variance of each repeat = its variance  × (1 − r²). 
###Four repeats × three markers × two sections = 24 estimates.
g <- function(z) loss_function_z4(z, pcna_A_cor)
result <- optim(rep(1.5, 4), g, method = "BFGS")
r_final <- tanh(result$par)
var_epsilon_pcnaA <- diag(pcna_A_cov) * (1 - r_final^2)

g <- function(z) loss_function_z4(z, vim_A_cor)
result <- optim(rep(1.5, 4), g, method = "BFGS")
r_final <- tanh(result$par)
var_epsilon_vimA <- diag(vim_A_cov) * (1 - r_final^2)

g <- function(z) loss_function_z4(z, tub_A_cor)
result <- optim(rep(1.5, 4), g, method = "BFGS")
r_final <- tanh(result$par)
var_epsilon_tubA <- diag(tub_A_cov) * (1 - r_final^2)

g <- function(z) loss_function_z4(z, pcna_B_cor)
result <- optim(rep(1.5, 4), g, method = "BFGS")
r_final <- tanh(result$par)
var_epsilon_pcnaB <- diag(pcna_B_cov) * (1 - r_final^2)

g <- function(z) loss_function_z4(z, vim_B_cor)
result <- optim(rep(1.5, 4), g, method = "BFGS")
r_final <- tanh(result$par)
var_epsilon_vimB <- diag(vim_B_cov) * (1 - r_final^2)

g <- function(z) loss_function_z4(z, tub_B_cor)
result <- optim(rep(1.5, 4), g, method = "BFGS")
r_final <- tanh(result$par)
var_epsilon_tubB <- diag(tub_B_cov) * (1 - r_final^2)

var_epsilon <- c(
  as.numeric(var_epsilon_pcnaA),
  as.numeric(var_epsilon_vimA),
  as.numeric(var_epsilon_tubA),
  as.numeric(var_epsilon_pcnaB),
  as.numeric(var_epsilon_vimB),
  as.numeric(var_epsilon_tubB)
)


### 3000 simulations: in each, every one of the 30 channels is assigned one of the 24 noise variances at random (with replacement), and the noise variance of each PC is the sum of channel noise variances weighted by squared loadings
loadings <- pca$rotation
a_sq     <- loadings^2
npc      <- ncol(loadings)
pc_var   <- pca$sdev^2

set.seed(1)
n_sim <- 3000

eps_pool <- var_epsilon[var_epsilon >= 0]
### each of the 30 markers is assigned one of the 24 noise variances at random.
draws     <- matrix(sample(eps_pool, n_sim * npc, replace = TRUE), nrow = n_sim)
sim_noise <- draws %*% a_sq
### predicted noise variance of a PC ÷ its observed variance
nf     <- sweep(sim_noise, 2, pc_var, "/")


### Summary of  noise fractions 
df <- data.frame(
  PC      = 1:npc,
  nf_mean = colMeans(nf),
  ### 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles across simulations
  ci_lo   = apply(nf, 2, quantile, 0.025),
  ci_hi   = apply(nf, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  var_explained = var_explained
)


###make Df for ploting fraction of varince explined by PC
var_explained_plot <- as.data.frame(var_explained) %>% 
  mutate(PC = 1:npc)

Noise_plot_tonsil_log_scale<- ggplot(df, aes(PC, nf_mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi), fill = "#FF474C", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(color = "red") +
  geom_point(color = "red", size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  ### Green line: fraction of total variance explained by each PC, for comparison with the predicted noise fractions.
  geom_line(aes(PC,var_explained),color = "darkgreen") +
    geom_point(aes(PC,var_explained),color = "darkgreen", size = 0.5) +

scale_y_log10(breaks = scales::log_breaks(n = 5), minor_breaks = scales::minor_breaks_n(10),
                labels = scales::label_log()) +
  labs(x = "PC", y = "Proportion of Variance") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.25),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(linewidth = 0.15)) 

print(Noise_plot_tonsil_log_scale)




ggsave("Data/noise_fraction_per_PC_log_scale.svg", plot = Noise_plot_tonsil_log_scale,
       width = 3, height = 2, units = "in",
       dpi = 300)  
```
